objective: Evaluating the deployed solution against the original business case and value proposition
secondaryObjectives: Analyzing and communicating identified gaps/deltas between solution scope, requirements, and what was actually built
Validating a solution's test results, reports, and evidence against requirements and acceptance criteria

sources.cite: PMI, Professional in Business Analysis (PMI-PBA) exam: Needs Assessment 18%, Planning 22%, Analysis 35%, Traceability and Monitoring 15%, Evaluation 10%
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 through summarizing fetches of two study pages: examcert.app (2026-08-16), which says its weights 'come from the current PMI exam outline', and masteryexamprep's PMI-PBA syllabus, which cites the PMI-PBA Handbook (revised 24 May 2022) and quotes tasks such as 'Initiate and document requirement changes using agreed change control processes and tooling' and 'Identify acceptance responsibilities (who accepts, evidence required, sign-off process) and align stakeholders'. Neither page quotes PMI's task statements on the requirements baseline; PMI's outline PDF was not opened. The objective wording is the course seed's, to verify. Reused for REQ-336 from this course's pmipba-claims-portal-baseline-signoff (the same reading and date); the objective wording is the course seed's.

The organization, the project, the figures and the people are fictional. The minutes or days each step takes and the effects of each decision are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.

brief.situation: You are the business analyst for a fictional engineering firm's new expense system, live for three months. The business case promised claims processed in 2 days instead of 9, and 1,200 finance hours saved a year.
handover: Finance reports 'it's working'. Some staff still submit paper claims.
The release deferred receipt scanning to a later phase.
howItWorks: The board shows the risk register against the appetite, each stakeholder's support in words and the docket.
Move on a week at a time. A decision comes to you at each review; before the first, you can read the evidence.
At the end you write the record and a short reflection.

then.log: Week 2: the CFO's budget assumes 1,200 hours saved and cuts two finance posts; claims back up to 11 days.
Week 3: a replacement project is scoped at 400 thousand dollars for a gap a 40 thousand dollar feature closes.
Week 4: receipt scanning is never scheduled; the promised savings never arrive.

reflection.question: Write the evaluation record for the sponsor.

parts.label: Value
parts.criteria: 4 days against 2; 700 hours against 1,200; caused by deferred receipt scanning.
parts.modelAnswer: Processing is 4 days against 2 and savings 700 hours against 1,200, because deferred receipt scanning keeps paper claims alive.

parts.label: Closure
parts.criteria: Phase one accepted on its criteria; the gap owned for phase two.
parts.modelAnswer: Phase one met its acceptance criteria; receipt scanning is recommended for phase two to close the gap.

scoring.modelReasoning: Solution evaluation compares the deployed solution's results with the business case's value proposition. Gaps between delivered scope and need are analyzed with evidence and communicated. Acceptance of a phase rests on its criteria and test evidence; value gaps are recorded and owned rather than dropped.
